notes.17: Candidates found this very difficult. All the agar blocks are stained uniformly. Therefore the original block of 1.0 cm × 1.0 cm × 1.0 cm will contain 1.0 cm3 of uniformly stained agar. A block 0.5 cm × 0.5 cm × 0.5 cm will contain 0.125 cm3 of uniformly stained agar. A block 0.5 cm × 1.0 cm × 1.0 cm will contain 0.5 cm3 of uniformly stained agar. A block 2.0 cm × 1.0 cm × 1.0 cm will contain 2.0 cm3 of uniformly stained agar. In the two options at 30°C, the volume of uniformly stained agar is the same as in the original block. Therefore the dye in the water will be at least the same colour as in the original experiment, if not darker blue. At 20°C in option B, there is only a quarter of the volume of uniformly stained agar, so as this diffuses out the water will be a lighter blue colour.
